title: Runtime Cost Governor — Product brief and Onboarding Playbook
author: Anika Shah
content:
Summary

Purpose: introduce the Runtime Cost Governor (RCG), a productized control plane that allows customers to define per-route and per-tenant cost governance policies that operate at inference runtime. The RCG balances latency, quality, and per-token spend by applying policy-driven adjustments (batching, quantization hints, fallback routing, and soft-fidelity nudges) in real time.

This document is both a product brief and an onboarding playbook: it explains goals and user value, outlines the runtime contract, and provides a step-by-step onboarding checklist for product, solutions, and SRE teams.

Background and motivation

Teams building production LLM features often face unpredictable inference spend spikes during bursts, model upgrades, or evaluation runs. Current levers (fixed pricing tiers, basic rate limits, and manual variant selection) are slow and coarse. The Runtime Cost Governor fills the gap by: 
- Providing programmatic, SLO-aware adjustments that run in the serving plane;
- Exposing a guardrail layer that ties economic controls to observed telemetry;
- Offering a developer-friendly surface for incremental rollout and customer opt-in.

Goals and success metrics

Primary goals:
1) Reduce unexpected per-tenant monthly spend variance by 30% within the first quarter of adoption for enterprise pilots.
2) Preserve 95% of routed traffic within configured latency SLOs when cost policies are active.
3) Provide clear billing explainability: every cost adjustment must be attributable in the console and billing reconciliations.

KPIs (Product & Ops):
- Spend variance reduction percentage per tenant
- Fraction of requests modified by RCG policies
- Median and p95 latency delta versus baseline
- Percentage of adjustments that triggered an alert or rollback

Target personas and use cases

Personas:
- Platform Engineer: configures tenant-level budget envelopes and emergency fallbacks.
- ML/Model Ops Engineer: defines fidelity tradeoffs and quantization-safe routing rules.
- Product Manager: establishes acceptable economic/quality tradeoffs for customers.
- Solutions Engineer: runs pilot onboarding and validates billing explainability.

Key use cases:
- Automatic backoff during bursty traffic to avoid budget overrun.
- Canaryed model upgrades with economic rollback triggers.
- Per-route negotiated discounts that consume from a budget pool with soft-fidelity enforcement.

High-level product behaviour and scope

What RCG does (in-scope):
- Apply per-request modifiers such as batch size hints, quantization profile selection, and fallback to cheaper variant based on policy predicates.
- Track a lightweight budget ledger per-tenant and per-route for enforcement and observability.
- Emit structured telemetry for billing reconciliation and explainability.

Out of scope for the initial release:
- Full automated re-pricing of contractual SLAs.
- Deep integration with external billing systems beyond tags and ledger exports.

Runtime contract and primitives (overview)

Policy primitives include budget envelopes, fidelity profiles, ordered fallback matrices, and enforcement modes. Policies are authored via Console or API and mirror a sanitized, versioned JSON schema. The policy surface exposes fields such as monthly credits, soft and hard threshold percentages, quantization profile names, and ordered variant lists.

SLOs, telemetry and billing mapping

SLO mapping (informational):
- Platinum: latency p95 target 150ms; contracted unlimited budget; minimal intervention.
- Gold: latency p95 target 250ms; moderate budget envelope; prefer medium quant.
- Silver: latency p95 target 400ms; conservative budget envelope; enforce fidelity reductions at high utilization.

Telemetry and explainability: every decision emitted by RCG includes request identifiers, tenant and route identifiers, pre-adjustment estimates for tokens and latency, the post-adjustment decision and realized cost delta, and a short reason code for the decision. This is surfaced in the Console and included in daily ledger exports to support reconciliation.

Implementation architecture (product view)

Components:
- Policy Engine (control plane): REST API and event stream, policy storage, versioning and UI.
- Runtime Adapter (serving plane extension): local evaluator that applies cached or real-time decisions in the request pipeline.
- Ledger Service: writes incremental token/credit consumption and produces daily exports.
- Console Integration: per-tenant dashboard for active policies, recent adjustments, and cost breakdowns.

Deployment models:
- Hosted: control plane in Redwood, adapters on serving nodes.
- Dedicated/Private: control plane optionally deployed into customer VPC as a managed connector, with ledger export sinks configurable by the customer.

Onboarding playbook (step-by-step)

1) Pre-sales discovery (Solutions and Sales)
   a) Document tenant goals: monthly budget target, acceptable latency delta, high-priority routes.
   b) Select an initial policy template from the policy library.

2) Pilot setup (Solutions and Platform) — suggested 2 week pilot
   a) Author policy via Console or API for the demo tenant.
   b) Enable runtime adapter on target routes with observe mode.
   c) Collect baseline telemetry for 48 to 72 hours.
   d) Run synthetic traffic scenarios to validate behavior under burst and canary conditions.

3) Controlled rollout (Platform and SRE)
   a) Transition policy from observe to warn for 72 hours and validate telemetry.
   b) Shift a small traffic percentage to enforce mode with automatic rollback triggers for latency and error rate regressions.
   c) Increase traffic exposure in phases while monitoring KPIs and cost metrics.

4) Production handover (Product and Customer Success)
   a) Finalize ledger export cadence and reconciliation plan with customer.
   b) Share expected billing impact samples and run a joint reconciliation exercise.
   c) Schedule a tuning retrospective 30 days after full rollout.

Operational playbook and runbook highlights

- Emergency mode: exceeding hard thresholds triggers emergency variant routing and alerts to tenant owner and SRE.
- Canary rollback: canary rules include economic drift and quality regression triggers that pause the rollout and create a ticket for Product investigation.
- Audit and reconciliation: daily ledger exports with schema versioning are required; nightly reconciliation jobs compare export totals to runtime counters.

Telemetry example (human-readable):
- timestamp: 2026-11-09T14:23:11Z; request_id: req-1234abcd; tenant: acme-corp; route: checkout-summary; policy: rcg-corp-demo; decision: fallback to small-8bit; cost_delta: -0.00068; reason: budget_soft_threshold_reached

Security and compliance notes

- Deploy Policy Engine inside customer VPC for private deployments; encrypt ledger exports with customer-managed keys.
- Audit logs for policy changes retained for 365 days.

Ownership and contacts

- Product owner: Anika Shah (product@redwood.ai)
- Engineering lead: Ravi Patel (serving-runtime)
- SRE contact: Maya Chen (eng-sre)

Roadmap: next 12 months (high level)

- Quarter 1 (post-launch): per-variant forecasting and interactive cost simulator in Console.
- Quarter 2: two-way ledger reconciliation integration with billing pipeline.
- Quarter 3: negotiated per-route commercial discounts and contract anchors.
- Quarter 4: embedded local-dev adapter for offline simulation and preflight tests.

Risks and mitigations

- Quality regressions due to aggressive policy enforcement: mitigate by defaulting to observe/warn and requiring canary for enforce transitions.
- Billing mismatches: mitigate with schema versioning, nightly reconciliation, and a developer-facing dispute flow.

Appendix: troubleshooting and CLI snippets

Troubleshooting checklist:
- Confirm runtime adapter version and control plane connectivity if adjustments are missing from telemetry.
- Verify ledger export pipeline if billing tags are missing.
- Pause policy and open an incident for latency regressions above configured thresholds.

Example CLI snippets (representative):
- Create policy: redwood rcg policies create --file rcg-policy-demo.json --tenant acme-corp
- Update enforcement: redwood rcg policies update rcg-corp-demo --enforcement enforce

FAQ (short)

Q: Does RCG change model weights or training artifacts?
A: No. RCG only modifies inference-time routing and execution knobs.

Q: How visible are cost adjustments to customers?
A: All adjustments are recorded in the Console and provided in daily ledger exports.

Q: Can customers opt out?
A: Policies are tenant-level and opt-in by default for hosted customers; private deployments can enable via a managed connector.
